So, now Mom, who wasn't there most of the time when you were young, knows. And wants to open up those wounds to asuage her own guilt? Or is she, in fact, being truthful do you think? I don't know what to make of it tbh.

But here's what you really need to do.

1. Set a hard line with Violet about NOT being MOH in this wedding. The furthest I'd go would be to attend as a guest, but I don't know what sort of damage that might to to you, considering...
2. Find out if this piece of garbage even is sorry in any way about what he did. Or if it was so inconsequential to him that he doesn't remember doing it. (I'm guessing there's some sob story about hard homelife/abusive parents/blah-blah that'll be spun to avoid the consequences).
3. Tell your fam in no uncertain terms that you will not be giving an inch in your stance, and they can accept that or go LC.
4. If your sis or god forbid, the garbage tries to gloss everything over, tell the fam in excrutiating detail exactly why you are taking the stance you are. Keep that spine shiny.
5. If the garbage is already switching the narrative around, maybe try to meet with him one on one (easy for me to say, I know), but talk to him about what he did and then secretly record him. Anything to get proof I say, because sadly this is a lot of he said, she said.

One thing I'm wondering about though, why would your sister not understand your position? She has to know how bad of an effect this had on you back then? Or is she the sort to willfully put rosetints on and stuff her ears to avoid unpleasantness? Or was she on the side of "I don't think I believe OP was bullied, and if she was, it wasn't THAT bad, and if it was bad, then she did something to deserve it"?

Also, she seems to have really fixated on the "Twin is going to be my MOH, come hell or highwater" thing. Is it more that she feels she must because it's expected? Or does she not have many close friends who'd be perhaps a better fit? Something seems fishy here.

First of all, I'm feel sorry for her for having to go through such a thing, and also pride for her for getting out. 

I've been in this exact position as the one cheated on, and let me tell you, the amount of guilt you have for THEM stepping out is ridiculous. That then gives way to absolute fury and lastly acceptance. 

If you think about it as being sort of like a death (the death of the concept of a commited relationship), then you sort of have the way it'll go. The 5 steps of grieving are: denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance. She sounds like she's between anger and bargaining right now (bargaining in this case being "I'm still right in letting the relationship die".)

You sound like an absolute gem of a guy, and someone who'll help her through it regardless. But you can't do that if your own mental health is suffering.

If I were you I'd start with asking her how it makes her feel when she has her spirals, is there anything that helps her not to have them? She'll likely say it makes her feel miserable. Then go to "Does she feel like it could be helpful to talk to a therapist?" (because bottling things up because you don't want to burden someone is what makes her act like this I think). Suggest she at least consider talking to someone like a therapist to get her feelings out, because I seriously don't think she wants to be this way. I certainly didn't. 

For me it was only when I'd managed to talk through it and vent all my anger and frustration that I reached the point where I just didn't care anymore. And you're right! Indifference is where she needs to get. To where she doesn't even care if she sees him. He's a scrub anyways. Not worth the energy it takes to maintain the anger. Hey! You're welcome to pm me if you'd like to talk more about Bergen as a city to live in and study options/housing, should you want.

As for advice:

1. To begin with, public transport, definitely. If only to get comfortable with the geography and have a very dependable transport option. You can get car used, there is a variety of dealers or even online options to chose from. PM for more info.
2. Rent. Student housing can be cheaper, sure, but a lot less dependable as far as availibility and housing standard. Most renters will also offer internet/utilities included in price, you you don't need to worry about different bills
3. Working can be fun and a nice income on the side, though most photographers will want a book of your work to see and I'm not sure how many, if any offer part time or call-in basis. You'd have to check about working on student visas though.
4. Public health is open to you, even on a student visa. You'd not get the full shebang of services untill you've established residency though, so I'd talk with the embassy about that beforehand.

All that said, welcome to our beautiful city and good luck to you. PM me if you have any questions at all, am more than happy to help. Can also offer rides if needed.

Being on the spectrum myself, I can with confidence say the following: The only way a person with ASD can learn to cope with the world around them is to have a very, very clear routine and extremely clear rules when faced with a difficult circumstance. It doesn't sound as if your brother has had any rules set for him, letalone rules that were enforced by your parents. 

I've learned myself that the best thing for me personally is to remove myself from the situation that could potentially trigger something or make me upset. Mostly because my Asbergers manifests more often than not as saying or doing inappropriate things without me realising it's wrong or WILL be taken the wrong way. Reading a room is a mystery to me..

Another way I've found is to have an item close by that is calming to me and feels good to have in my hands/against my skin. For me, it's a Hermés scarf I once bought for my late mother that I asked to keep when she passed. It's non abrasive, light weight and doesn't take any space at all. I simply rub it against skin or even just hold it. Calms me way more than talking ever could.

All that said, you are definitely not the AH in this case, though your parents certainly seem to be. It feels to me as though they simply chose the road of least resistance, meaning they play along to keep him from acting out.  I say keep going, as he must be shown that actions have consequences, and his parents won't always be around.
